ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an organic transition-state structure; on the left there is a benzene ring, and the benzene ring is connected to a positively charged NH2 group; this nitrogen is further connected to the central carbon. The central carbon is connected upward to an upper carbon, and connected down to the right to an OEt substituent. The upper carbon is connected on the left to an EtO2C substituent, and on the upper right to an ester/enolate unit containing O− and OEt. There are also multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows, and bonds involving hydrogen are not counted. Counting reasoning: Count the bonds between heavy atoms by fragments. The benzene ring has 6 C-C bonds in total. The phenyl-N bond and the N-central carbon bond total 2. The central carbon-upper carbon bond is 1. The OEt substituent down to the right of the central carbon contains central C-O, O-CH2, and CH2-CH3, for a total of 3. The left EtO2C substituent contains upper C-carbonyl C, C=O, C-O, O-CH2, and CH2-CH3, for a total of 5. The top/right enolate ester unit contains upper C=top C, top C-O−, top C-OEt, O-CH2, and CH2-CH3, for a total of 5. The total is 6 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 5 + 5 = 22.

Count the left EtO2C substituent as upper C-carbonyl C, C=O, C-O, O-CH2, and CH2-CH3: 5. Count the top/right enolate ester unit as upper C=top C, top C-O−, top C-OEt, O-CH2, and CH2-CH3: 5. Sum 6+2+1+3+5+5 = 22.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a heavy-atom graph, ignoring arrows and H atoms, then compute by degrees. The phenyl ring contributes heavy-atom degrees 13: five ring carbons have degree 2 and the ipso carbon bonded to N has degree 3. The N has degree 2. The central carbon has degree 3. The upper carbon joining the central carbon, EtO2C carbonyl carbon, and top/right carbon has degree 3. The lower OEt branch contributes degrees 2+2+1 = 5 for O, CH2, CH3. The left EtO2C group contributes degrees 3+1+2+2+1 = 9 for carbonyl C, carbonyl O, ester O, ethyl CH2, ethyl CH3. The top/right O−/OEt carbon unit contributes degrees 3+1+2+2+1 = 9. Total degree sum is 13+2+3+3+5+9+9 = 44, so the number of heavy-heavy bonds is 44/2 = 22.
